notes.title: [BETA] CHANGELOG| 1.1.78_a
notes.content:
Hi everyone,
here is the latest update. It's released on the BETA branch as we couldn't reproduce some bugs. We would be grateful for your feedback and information when you encounter problems or any issues. 

[h3]Changelog 1.1.78_a[/h3]
[quote]
[list]
[*]A reputation system has been added between the player and the NPC at sea. When a player has a low reputation among the NPCs, he will not help us or charge more for hauling away. The reputation between the NPCs can be viewed in the tablet in the scoreboard
[*]Added The ability to tow NPC ships to the port
[*]Added the option to grind the bait by crew members (they take the bait themselves from the fridge and grind it)
[*]Storm mechanics added. Storms occur in specific areas and move according to the direction of the wind. Swimming in will take damage and sink.
[*]Land and shoals added
[*]The option to receive radio messages has been added. After receiving it, it shows us the appropriate menu
[*]Added ship speed up option in debugger options to check for errors
[*]Added more information about the current crew status on the UI
[*]Added an option for the player to push the crew back for critical situations when they get stuck somewhere
[*]Fixed a bug with the ground information not being displayed on the map
[*]Fixed a bug with the crew catching frames
[*]Fixed a bug with NPCs that were influencing the land
[*]Fixed NPCs dropping frames
[*]The infinite world has been improved
[*]Fixed bolsters in the port
[*]Improved the sound of the feet in the port
[*]Improved game performance at sea
[*]Crew animation has been improved
[*]Fixed a bug with the second steak not being visible in the ship select screen
[*]Fixed the bug with the Crew panel overlap on the tablet map
[*]The icons on the sorting table have been improved
[*]Fixed a bug with the crewman throwing the hook
[*]Improved the transparency of the control panel (letters are better visible)
[*]The ship may become immobilized ashore
[*]Improved texture settings for buildings in the port
[*]Reduced-intensity of illumination (overexposure)
[*]The player can call for help by radio in order to be towed to the port
[*]The wind direction is displayed on the monitor at the helm
[*]The game world for terrain operation has been reduced and adjusted, fuel consumption, map distances, and enemy positions[/list][/quote]

[BETA] Update 1.1.1

New developer! New features! New Roadmap!
notes.content:
Hello everyone,
today I would like to inform that Deadliest Catch: The Game will receive a new developer who will provide further support for the game including debugging (including existing bugs) and adding many new features! 

It will not be fast or slow - the speed at which fixes will be made will depend on the amount of work that awaits us all. We would like to provide you with everything as quickly as possible, but we do not want to repeat the mistakes.

If you are curious what awaits you, below you will find a full list of planned features called [b]Roadmap.[/b] Please remember that dates may change - some things may be earlier and others later!

[h1]Roadmap[/h1]
[quote]
[h2]MILESTONE 1 (EST 30.06.2020)[/h2]
[olist][*] Analyze the source or output code and organize it for easier and faster implementation of new features.
[*] Increase the performance of the Game.
[*] Added a 3D F/V Northwestern ship model to the Game in the form of a free DLC.
[*] Adding the ability to select a ship in the port (currently it's only on the campaign creation screen).
[*] Remove any bugs in the game that will be revealed during the milestone development.
[/olist]

[h2]MILESTONE 2 (EST 31.07.2020)[/h2]
[olist][*] Eliminate bugs detected by QA PLW/ULG teams and make appropriate adjustments to allow players to play smoothly.
[*] Adding to the Game a fully functional wheel-house (currently only partially made): [list]
[*] Adding radio and radio support from the port e.g. "WARNING, A storm is coming" or "MEIDEI MEIDEI and coordinates concerning the ship which calls for assistance);
[*] Add interactive monitors to show your current location on the map and water temperature/depth
[*] The ability to walk around the control room (currently the player is closed and glued to the chair),
[*] Addition of other controls.[/list]
[*] Improving the system of the randomness of the occurrence and catch of crabs, so that the player despite the use of the best baits does not always catch the same amount of crabs, ie:
Crabs occur randomly on the map relative to environmental parameters:[list]
[*] Water temperature,
[*] Depth,
[*] Type of substrate.[/list]
[*] Remove any bugs in the game that will be revealed during the milestone development.
[*] Addition of new crab species
[/olist]

[h2]MILESTONE 3 (EST 31.08.2020)[/h2]
[olist]
[*] Improving crew performance:[list]
[*] Animations,
[*] The smoothness of tasks performed,[/list]
[*] Added the possibility of switching off the engine in the boat.
[*] Adding to the Game other animals that appear randomly in the environment, i.e.: Whales, orcas, seagulls, albatross or seals.
[*] Adding to the Game, fish or other animals that:[list]
[*] can be caught in cages,
[*] can be converted into the bait,
[*] may be thrown overboard.[/list]
[*] Remove any bugs in the game that will be revealed during the milestone development.
[*] Adding ship damage to the Game:[list]
[*] the possibility of the ship overturning during a storm,
[*] the possibility of entering the shallows,
[*] the possibility of sinking the ship by hitting another ship/iceberg.[/list]
[/olist]

[h2]MILESTONE 4 (EST 30.09.2020)[/h2]
[olist]
[*] Adding the ability to walk around the port and visit all the points i.e. shop, office, processing,
[*] bar. The player can get off the ship himself and enter it <wooden footbridge>.
[*] Adding objects at sea in the form of icebergs, shallows (shallows) and coastline visible during
[*] swimming, to which the player can sail.
[*] Remove any bugs in the game that will be revealed during the milestone development.
[*] Addition of competition ships based on the ship models currently available in the game:[list]
[*] Ships are to be visible by the player while swimming,
[*] Ships throw their buoys and cages into the sea,
[*] The player can interact with ships, i.e.:[list]
[*] damage, sinking the ship;
[*] pulling out not your buoys/pots (theft = penalty);
[*] towing the damaged vessel.[/list][/list]
[/olist][/quote]

notes.title: [BETA] Game Update 1.0.6 / Beta / Steam cards
notes.content:
Hello everyone,
as you may know, we have a severe issue with save&load system and loading times. We were unable to localize the problem and we are tracking it for 4 days. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33963706/9887753df0f137e4372affddff040f4e8c2739a1.jpg[/img]

Unfortunately, update 1.0.5 didn't solve anything and caused more issues as players reported. That is why we decided to launch a parallel branch called "BETA". You will be able to choose its in-game properties tab. Below you will find more information. 

[h1]BETA[/h1]

notes.title: Development Progress - update note
notes.content:
[b]Ahoy fearless Captains![/b]

Today we’d like to tell you a little about our current focus and the upcoming features, that will get implemented in Deadliest Catch: The Game. So here’s what we’ve been up to. :)

Recently, we’ve been working on the major update for one of the most important features - the crew management system. As you all well know, currently there are three workers available, each performing a specific task. With the upcoming update, we are going to put much more decisions in your hands, captains!

First of all, we will provide you with a very useful tool to manage your ship - the tablet. Within the tablet, there will be a special panel designed to manage your crew. There you will be able to see your available crewmen and assign them to tasks of your choice. All the actions will be connected with “work loops” - either preparing the pots or collecting pots from the water (the third loop for your sailors is resting). While your crew is working on their assignments, you can check the progress of each task on the tablet.

After this major update, we will be developing the tablet feature furthermore, including the full information panel within it, for example helping you keep track of all your items in the storage or the issued fines. In time, the tablet will become a true command center of your vessel. :)

When we got the tablet figure out, we’ll proceed to develop another awaited features - progression. We intend to implement multiple seasons, so all the money and resources you’ve gathered will pass between them. The same goes for the upgrades and captain’s skills (more of those will be available in the future). So that’s how your career in crab fishing goes!

See you soon on the Bering Sea!

notes.title: Deadliest Catch: The Game - Early Access Release
notes.content:
[h1]Everyone on BOARD!!![/h1]

[b]An important day for our game is here! Today, November the 14th, we released Deadliest Catch: The Game in the Early Access on Steam! From now on you can purchase and play our game via Steam and participate in creating it by your feedback. :)[/b]

Like we’ve done many times before, we’d like to start with a huge thank you to our community - all the Kickstarter backers, pre-alpha testers, members of our Discord server. Your involvement, support, and feedback have been (and still are!) a tremendous help to us all. We are sure that we wouldn’t be able to do many, many things with this project if it wasn’t for you all! :)

That being said, let’s now focus on the Early Access release itself. So what has changed in comparison to the demo version that you were able to play up to this point? First of all, we implemented two important features that you were often asking about - save system and the full tutorial. As for the crew management system, the main goal of our successful Kickstarter Campaign, we are starting with the basic version of it and we will keep developing it during the Early Access period.

We expect the Early Access to last about 4 to 6 months, mostly depending on the progress with the development. Our main short-term goals for the first weeks will be polishing the current state of the game and fixing bugs reported by players and beta-testers, as well as looking into the matters pointed to us during the Kickstarter Campaign. From there on, we intend to focus on the equipment wearing off and the dynamic mechanics of the fisheries; as well as captain’s tablet that will help you manage your ship, crew, and skills (starting with the basic version of it).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33963706/aff40968beb74339c4d15f299f4250057c788f56.jpg[/img]

But we have a lot more on the horizon. :) We’d like to bring your captain’s experience to the new level with a career mode consisting of the consequent seasons in which you will upgrade your ship and gain new skills while earning money and catching up to the AI competition. There will be a bunch of cosmetic changes, like setting the name of your captain, ship, and ship’s coloring presets; fully functional wheelhouse (with some changeable music on the radio); all the cool Kickstarter rewards (like hidden in-game messages); a pop-up information system, that will keep you posted on the situation on the Bering Sea and so on. In the meantime, we will be doing localization for various languages.

As we stated earlier, the crew system - probably the most anticipated feature - will get enriched in the future updates. We want to implement a fatigue system that will make managing your crew more advanced. Then the next step will be improving the employment system (for example allowing you to pay your crew a share of your income). Finally, we intend to make the Bering Sea more dangerous (and the catch more deadly). Waves, equipment malfunctions, ship damage … and possibly some accidents that can occur to the crewmembers.

You can check the planned Development Road Map for Deadliest Catch: The Game [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/838630/discussions/0/1639802081893080787/]HERE.[/url]

Of course, we will keep you posted about the updates and the changes implemented in them. Please let us know what you think by leaving recommendations and comments on the Steam discussion pages. If you haven’t joined our Discord server yet - [url=https://discord.gg/zwTX9Mb][b]go for it :)[/b][/url] It’s the best place to share your feedback or ask questions about games! Also, please report to us all the bugs you’ve encountered. The game is still in the development and some problems may (and probably will) happen at first - but we’ll do our best to deal with them as soon as we can. 

[b]See you at the Bering Sea, Captains![/b]

notes.title: Devlog #4 - The Bait
notes.content:
[h1]Ahoy brave Captains![/h1]

It’s time to share with you some fresh details of our progress with the development of the game, so here goes the brand new Devlog! This time we will tell you a little about the bait - rest assured, it’s not a click-bait though, we will discuss the actual, yummy stuff.  Well... yummy for the crabs at least :)

Let’s start with some facts about our favorite sea creatures. As you may know, the crabs have an excellent sense of smell and they use it to find food - when they feel the scent of something delicious (or just acceptable - crabs’ taste is not very refined, to be honest), they will find it and dig it out of seabed or snatch it with their claws. Knowing that we can guess that some pungent bait should attract crabs perfectly. An interesting fact: not only the scent can lure the crabs towards the food, but also the sounds of other crabs already feasting on it. So once some crabs walk right into our pot, there is a good chance for a “chain reaction”. ;)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33963706/53981503b0ad003362cffdbb136b1873ded023e1.png[/img]

Appealing to the crabs’ sense of smell is the main idea behind the baits used by the fisherman. Although the scent needs to be intense, so it can reach crabs spread on wide territory, it’s important not to overdo it. The old, smelly fish may seem like a tempting choice in that case, but it probably won’t be as effective as we may think. Crabs can easily tell the fresh food from the old and rancid one and they will obviously choose the first one. So here’s the ground rule - “fresh bait is always the best”.

Real-life fishermen use many different kinds of fish (and not only) to prepare their bait. Fish carcass, shad, herring, clams, mink, chicken, turkey… you name it. But do crabs have some sweet-tooth for a certain kind of meat? Sure they do ;) The Red King crabs are usually baited with saury, squid, herring, sardines, and cod. When catching Opilios, on the other hand, the most popular option is the squid - it’s meat is tougher and doesn’t get devoured by sand fleas, that can live in the locations with the sandy seabed.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33963706/ff482bbe1b693c273b8b84c236855685d485a34a.png[/img]

Now let’s talk about our approach towards the in-game baits and how exactly do they work. There are two main types of baits in Deadliest Catch: The Game - the frozen blocks of fish (saury, squid, herring and sardines) and the raw fish (cod). All baits have two parameters that will affect the outcome of our fishing efforts. Those are freshness and aromaticity. The freshness indicates how strong a given bait will attract the nearby crabs, while aromaticity influences the range, from which crabs can sense it.

We stated earlier, that the fresh meat is always better (form the crabs’ point of view for sure), but when on a boat we need to make some compromises. The dilemma of frozen vs raw bait connects to those two parameters we mentioned. The frozen bait stays appealing to the crabs for a longer period of time - either when it’s stored on the vessel or already thrown into the pot. On the other hand, it’s less aromatic. With the raw fish, it’s the other way around - it has much more aromaticity, but will go bad faster. It’s up to you Captains to figure out how to deal with them in the most efficient way! :)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33963706/e75cd12c82a79835cf30e1c596c3d815f155ef45.png[/img]

The frozen and raw bait goes in the pots in different ways too. The first one often referred to as a jar bait, is stored in big blocks. Such block needs to get shredded in the grinder - the portions of minced fish fill the plastic jar that is placed in the pot afterwards. Such jars are not only containing the bait - they are releasing it slowly, so the crabs already trapped in pot don’t eat everything right away. You can prepare more jars beforehand and store them in the freezer, and they are eco-friendly and reusable. :) The raw fish - also known as a hang bait, goes directly into the pot. Although it is much more aromatic, it gets devoured pretty quickly by the crabs - first comes, first served.

In the demo version of Deadliest Catch: The Game you could only use the bait jars - but in the full version of the game, both frozen and raw bait will be available. Balancing the freshness and aromaticity of those two kinds of bait will allow you to come up with the most efficient combinations. Rember, that you can put both kinds in the same pot!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33963706/ac01e293fd800c1a178ef8e42b0b421c7906dbab.png[/img]

That’s about it on the bait topic. ;) We hope that you enjoyed our new Devlog and soon we will be returning with more insights from our development team! Don’t forget to join our [url=https://discord.gg/zwTX9Mb]Discord server[/url] and see you soon!

Don’t forget to check the notification icon on top![/b]

[img]https://i.imgur.com/yTFKj6u.gif[/img]

As we promised, the main goal of the campaign will be implementing the crew management mechanics in its basic form. When you’ll hire a crewman, you’ll be able to assign him to a chosen task on deck - for example setting the pots or sorting the caught crabs. As he’ll keep performing the given task, he’ll get better at his job, doing it faster and more efficient. Additionally, when the crewman will be free for the moment, he’ll perform secondary actions, like preparing the bait or repairing the equipment.

We have some additional features planned from the start, so they make a place in the stretch-goal list. Among them you can find improvement of the crew management mechanics (f.e. the crewmen will get tired as they work on deck) or equipment upgrades. We’ve also included one of the big features that you were oftenly asking about - the multiplayer mode! :)

[img]https://i.imgur.com/fc8L7ox.gif[/img]

As for the campaign rewards, we’ve prepared multiple options for you. From getting copy of the game at a better price, through access to beta-tests and digital posters, to exclusive rewards like placing hidden objects in the game or naming a captain after you - we’ve got you covered. In any case, look out for the limited early-bird (or in our case, the early-crab) rewards, cause you’ll be able to get a sweet deal out of them.

We hope that you are as hyped for this campaign as we are - please share the good news with your friends and if you have any questions, don’t hesitate to ask them here! :)

notes.title: The Crew and Kickstarter plans
notes.content:
[h1]Hello DC Fans![/h1]

Today we’d like to talk about the topic, that has been repeatedly appearing in comments and discussions on the Steam page and social media. The element of the game, that is clearly very important and crucial for you - [b]the crew.[/b]

To be honest, when we started working on a game, we decided to go with gameplay mechanics in the All-in-One system. While playing the game, you’ll have to do every task by yourself and accurate simulation of all those activities will be the core gameplay. One of the key arguments for this approach was the budget. Implementing the crew requires a lot of additional work for our team - programming, creating models and textures, animating, etc. That means more time and more costs needed for finishing the game.

So, when we first saw comments about the lack of crew mechanics, we were reluctant to switch our focus, knowing that we might not be able to deliver that big of a feature. But we are gamers ourselves, and what we want the most is to bring you joy and great experience. And you really convinced us that this game needs the crew, so we’ll do our best to implement it. But - we can’t do it without your help.

[b]We decided, that the best solution will be going with Deadliest Catch: The Game on Kickstarter - and making implementation of the crew the main goal of the campaign.[/b] That way, with your help, we can gather funds necessary for the production and create the game you are all waiting for! We have a lot of ideas of the stretch goals too - many of those appearing in the comments or discussions. 

We hope that together we'll be able to make this game just the way you’d hope - truly bringing your favorite TV series to your PCs and letting you feel like fishing on the Bering Sea by yourselves. Surely with your support we can do it!

At this moment we plan to start the Kickstarter Campaign around half of the April - soon we’ll come back to you with more details. Let us know what do you think about that!

notes.title: Devlog #3 - The Red King Crabs
notes.content:
[h1]Ahoy captains![/h1] 

After the first two issues of our devlogs, you should know all the basics of your F/V and equipment on board. This time we’d like to move to the most important part of the titular Deadliest Catch - the catch itself! In other words,  the precious crabs that you’ll try to fish out of hazardous waters of the Bering Sea. Though many of you, devoted fans of the Discovery Channel series, have a great knowledge of crabs living in Alaskan waters, we’d like to sum-up some facts and share with you how we implemented that information in our game.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33963706/0cf34d1961fce2c232c0790cedceb4cf1879de48.jpg[/img]

Right now we’d like to focus on one of the crab’s species that are caught by the fisherman in the TV series - the [b]red king crabs[/b] (Paralithodes camtschaticus). The first thing you’ll need to know about them is that they are rather big creatures. The fully grown males can have up to 11 inches/28 cm in length of the carapace (the shell covering the back) and leg span as big as 5 foots/150 cm. With five pairs of legs and huge claws, you’d better be careful when handling them!

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33963706/5bcf73410f3da148f3dcf33da9e7435c156da725.jpg[/img]

The second important fact is that not all crabs are suitable for sale! It is allowed to catch only the male crabs that are old enough. That’s why all the crabs trapped in the pots go directly to the sorting table, where you’ll have to decide, which crabs will go to your holding tank (and will be later sold in Dutch Harbor), and which will need to be tossed back into the water. So how can you check your catch?

The first thing to consider is the crab’s sex. Looking from the above, both males and females looks quite alike. However, when you’ll look at their abdomens, you can see a so-called abdominal flap. The male specimens have a narrow flap, while the female’s flap is wide - it covers most of the underside of the abdomen (that’s because female crabs carry their eggs under the flap). The other thing that helps to distinguish males from females is their size, as the males are usually bigger. The crab’s size is used to judge the age of the crabs as well. Crabs suitable for sale have to be at least 6,5 inch/17 cm in carapace length.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/m8Fx1Y1.gif[/img]

Inspecting the crabs in our game is quite simple. First, you’ll need to pick up one of the caught crabs and turn it around. Observing the crab’s abdominal will tell you about the specimen’s sex and further inspection will show, whether the crab is big enough. That information will appear in your GUI. It’s not necessary to wait for the result of the inspection - after a while, you can judge in a glimpse of an eye which crab should go under the deck and which will be tossed overboard. But be careful! If you try to sell a crab, that shouldn’t go on the market, you’ll have to pay a fine.

It’s important to control the amount of the crabs that you hold in your tank as well. The weight of the crabs will burden your F/V and if the tank gets too crowded, it’ll cause the crabs to die. And dead crab in your tank may cause other surrounding crabs to die quicker (that so-called “dead loss” will bring you no income of course). So if you fill your tank faster than you expected, it may be advised to return to the dock even in the middle of the season.

So that’s a little factsheet about the red king crabs. Let us know if there is some information that you are most interested in reading next time :) See you soon!

notes.title: Devlog #2 - The equipment
notes.content:
[h1]Ahoy captains![/h1]

So last time we get a good look at your very own vessel. It’s time to get familiar with all the fishing equipment on board and the purpose that they serve. All of the machines and items are essential to your work on the F/V. The better you’ll learn to use them, the more crabs you’ll catch and eventually sell back in the Dutch Harbour. So let’s get on with this!

[img]https://i.imgur.com/X2CxjGo.gif[/img]

Our first stop is [b]the crane[/b]. It’s definitely the biggest (and highest) machine you’ll use on your F/V. It is hydraulicly lifted and helps you with moving the empty crab pots from the deck on to [b]the launcher[/b] and back. At the end of the crane’s arm, you can see a tire, that prevents the crab pots from getting damaged while being moved by the crane.

With [b]the crab pot[/b] set on the launcher, it’s time to prepare it before tossing overboard. First, you’ll need to take the rope with the attached buoys out of the pot (moving it on top of the cage) and place a bait bag inside. The set pot can be thrown into the water with the launcher - it is operated with a lever next to the machine. The crab pot will stay in the water for the next 24-48 hours, luring precious king crabs inside with the delicious bait (delicious to the crabs at least).

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33963706/768459ad2e92411dd286de32b721a3960c4d9be3.jpg[/img]

But, the said bait needs to get prepared first too. That’s when [b]the fridge[/b] and [b]the bait chopper[/b] will come in handy. In the fridge standing on the F/V deck, you’ll keep all the blocks of frozen fish that you bought before leaving the Dutch Harbor (they come in many kinds, but that’s a story for another time). You’ll throw those blocks into the chopper - better watch out for hands! - and take out the bait ready to get bagged and placed in the crab pot.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/9t4JfNd.gif[/img]

When the pot is full of crabs (or at least you’ll think it is) you’ll need to get it out of the water - and that can get a little complicated. First, you’ll need [b]the throwing hook[/b] to get the rope attached to the pot out of the water and in your hands. It’s a moment to test your manual skills, as you’ll have to throw the hook between the buoys and pull it in your direction.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33963706/393948c1528fdae2d0479fba3435cd368bcb79b2.jpg[/img]

When you’ll get a rope, you should place it on [b]the hauling system[/b]. With the crab pot close to the fishing vessel's board, you’ll need to grab it with [b]the picking hook[/b] and use [b]the picking boom[/b] to set the full pot back on the launcher. The launcher can tilt in two directions, so this time it’ll help you with throwing crabs on [b]the automatic sorting table[/b] from the pot - so you can look closely at what got caught in your trap. All the big, tasty male crabs go down to[b] the holding tank [/b]through [b]the hatch[/b]. Uff.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/Io8sQrX.gif[/img]

So now you know what your everyday work at the deck will look like - or the basics of it, to be precise! Soon we’ll continue with our devlogs and take a better look at the crabs. In the meantime let us know what you think about our work and the devlog itself. And if you didn’t do it yet - don’t hesitate to add Deadliest Catch: The Game to your wishlist! 
See you soon!

notes.title: Devlog #1 - The fishing vessel
notes.content:
[h1]Ahoy brave Captains![/h1]

We - the development team of [i]Deadliest Catch: The Game[/i] - are really excited to see your interest and anticipation for the game release. We are also receiving many questions and suggestions from you about the game content and your expectations regarding it. That’s why we decided to create a series of devlogs in which we’ll share with you some insights from our work on this title. We hope that you’ll enjoy reading it!

That being said, are you ready to step into the wheelhouse of your own ship and set course on the deadly Alaskan waters? Let’s make sail than! And what’s a better thing to start with than the fishing vessel itself?

[img]https://i.imgur.com/BO700j5.gif[/img]

While playing the game, you’ll become the owner of a crab fishing vessel with all the equipment essential for catching the precious king crabs and bringing them safely to the Dutch Harbor. The design of the ship is based on the boat well-known from the Discovery Channel show - F/V Cornelia Marie. It’s approximately 42 meters long, 10 meters width and 20 meters high (counting to the top of the mast). Let’s take a quick tour of it!

[b]The deck [/b]is where the magic happens. Here you can find all the important equipment like the hydraulically lifted crane, empty crab pots, the coiler, the lift, the sorting table, the bait-cutting machine, the fridge for the bait and basket with buoys. The deck is where you will spend most of your in-game time. Better get familiar with it! From the deck, you can also access all the other parts of the vessel.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33963706/b26904e2be541fb68058878ec1e6e523fb0514d1.jpg[/img]

[b]In the storage room[/b], you’ll keep all the additional items that may come in handy. Spare grappling hooks, the hydraulic oil or repair kits to maintain the equipment. Provided, that you remembered to buy it all before leaving the port for the season!

Under the deck, there is [b]the holding tank[/b] filled with salt water. That’s where all the crabs suitable for sale are kept while your vessel is at sea. Remember, that you have to deliver the crabs alive, otherwise nobody will buy them and all your hard work will go to waste. But don’t get greedy - there is a limited amount of crabs you can safely fit in the tank. If you allow your vessel to get overburden (and that means the weight of pots, fuel, additional equipment and obviously the caught crabs), it’ll affect the mileage and make steering more difficult.

[b]The wheelhouse[/b] allows you to truly take command of your vessel. Literally - from this place you can steer the ship. There are four speed-levels for going forward and one for reverse movement. What’s important, you can set the engine power to the desired level and leave the wheelhouse to drop the pots or sort the caught crabs - the vessel will proceed sailing in the set direction. From the wheelhouse, you can also switch on the map and set course to the previously chosen points in the fast-travel mode.

Finally, you can visit [b]the upper deck[/b]. From there you can admire the sight of splendid but treacherous Bering Sea!

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33963706/cf3a79b5cb92896c4034c331529f2bf5778f8e56.jpg[/img]

Now you know what you might expect on board of your own fishing vessel. Soon we’ll give you a little more details about the equipment you’ll get to use during your adventure. Let us know what do you think about our ideas and the devlog itself. Also, tell us if there are topics that you’d especially like to read about in the future. See you soon, captains!
